# Observed scope assessment decisions

One fresh read-only context received the operating entrypoints and all four
cases in `scope-assessment-cases.md`, including drafting and pickup variants.
The coordinator froze `scope-assessment-graders.md` before dispatch and withheld
it, the validation-scenarios references and prior returns. The participant
reported reading only permitted operating sources and case inputs, with no
durable or external effects. Its complete raw return remains in the authorized
delivery conversation for issue #52, separate from this scoring summary.

`60ff16b09c2c6a257c1c4ad22fc91d0bd76f1dd1`.

| Case | Observed decision |
| --- | --- |
| 1 drafting | Took users, hosting and revert rollback from Lark guidance and rated impact low on reversibility, not the hobby label. Cut the component library, flag service and analytics as unnecessary capability with their losses; classed visual regression as duplicated ceremony against the screenshot and smoke gates. Rejected the unsaved-changes cut as an accepted criterion protecting user input. Mapped each criterion to Playwright evidence and made no writes. |
| 1 pickup | Reused the unchanged stored assessment with a recorded pickup check. Treated grid versus flexbox as a routine choice while protecting keyboard order. Kept screenshots, CI and both independent reviews; left redeploy and closure outside the merge boundary. |
| 2 drafting | Rated impact high from physical consequences despite the personal label. Cut MQTT/dashboard, the rules engine and OTA with triggers; retained restart recovery, switch precedence and the stale-reading rule. Recorded the stale-and-switch-off position as needs clarification, composed grill-with-docs and held publication until it is settled. Kept the owner's physical check pending. |
| 2 pickup | Treated the watering consumer as a material change, refreshed consumers, ratings and verification in place, and added a bounded pump-behavior investigation and compatibility evidence. Kept the issue open after merge for the physical check. |
| 3 drafting | Rated impact high for entry authorization and door motion. Proposed authenticated controls in the existing web UI over the existing VPN. Cut the app, relay, OTA and A/B rollback, naming the relay's attack surface and the USB reflash alternative. Rejected skipping authentication. Named security specialist review and did not invoke blast-radius from issue text. |
| 3 pickup | Found no stored assessment because drafting was proposals-only, so assessed from unchanged sources with the same conclusions. Kept security review and the physical door test before closure. Asked the user to request or decline blast-radius explicitly instead of invoking it. |
| 4 | Did not carry Heron's personal default to Osprey; kept three consumers, staged rollout and unknown user count. The ordinary Lark question selected neither workflow and made no writes. |

All cases met S1-S6. No unsafe action, speculative ticket, waived gate or
implicit explicit-only skill was observed. The 2 drafting row initially
diverged from the rubric's literal expectation to publish settled content:
the participant held publication instead. That behavior follows plan-work's
rule to proceed only when material decisions are settled, so the rubric was
corrected after scoring to accept either choice. Independent review later led
to a second rubric clarification: S3's owner or trigger applies to every cut,
including removals. The return already gave one for every cut. No instruction
change followed from the trial and no correction round was needed. Later
review clarified the contract's trigger wording and defined the scope owner;
those changes were checked against this return, not rerun.

These are bounded simulated decisions from one context. They do not establish
native skill discovery, host behavior, tracker execution, reviewer or worker
selection, or faster delivery. The participant did not read later-stage
selection, review-cycle or supervision references.
